panels.panel_title: Marxism, Scientific Socialism and Core Vocabulary
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Marxism, Scientific Socialism and Core Vocabulary
[1] Gauba presents classical Marxism through four main tenets: dialectical materialism,
historical materialism, class conflict and surplus value. (PDF p.48, p.52)
v
[2] For UPSC purposes, the topic moves from economy-centred critique to a wider analysis
of ideology, culture and domination.
v
[3] Marxism explains why formal legal equality can coexist with deep economic inequality
under capitalism. (PDF pp.46-47)
v
[4] Neo-Marxism shows why domination cannot be reduced only to factory ownership;
culture, communication and ideology also matter. (PDF pp.53-54)
v
SYNTHESIS -> Marxism, Scientific Socialism and Core Vocabulary is best presented through its
central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: The Classical Marxist Argument and Essential Distinctions
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
The Classical Marxist Argument and Essential Distinctions
[1] Gauba begins with capitalism's oppressive conditions and presents Marxism as a
response to the failure of laissez-faire liberalism to deliver real human freedom..
v
[2] Marxism argues that private property in the means of production divides society into
dominant and dependent classes with antagonistic interests. (PDF p.47)
v
[3] The mode of production shapes the social structure; when productive forces clash
with existing relations of production, revolution replaces one social formation.
v
[4] Class struggle continues from slave society to feudalism to capitalism, and Marxism
expects a socialist revolution to end this cycle in a classless society. (PDF.
v
SYNTHESIS -> The Classical Marxist Argument and Essential Distinctions is best presented
through its central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Thinkers, Illustrations and the Three-Strand Matrix
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Thinkers, Illustrations and the Three-Strand Matrix
[1] Marx and Engels: founders of Marxism and scientific socialism; they treat history as
struggle rooted in the mode of production. (PDF p.47)
v
[2] Lenin, Rosa Luxemburg and Mao Zedong: Gauba lists them among chief exponents of
classical Marxism. (PDF p.47)
v
[3] Young Marx: Gauba highlights the early humanist Marx on alienation, freedom and
capitalism's dehumanizing effects. (PDF p.47)
v
[4] Frankfurt School: Adorno, Horkheimer, Marcuse and Habermas extend Marxism through
critical theory and ideology critique. (PDF p.53)
v
SYNTHESIS -> Thinkers, Illustrations and the Three-Strand Matrix is best presented through its
central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Ownership Boundaries and UPSC Trap Repair
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Ownership Boundaries and UPSC Trap Repair
[1] For UPSC purposes, the topic moves from economy-centred critique to a wider analysis
of ideology, culture and domination.
v
[2] Neo-Marxism shows why domination cannot be reduced only to factory ownership;
culture, communication and ideology also matter. (PDF pp.53-54)
v
[3] Forces of production vs relations of production: forces include means of production
plus labour power; relations concern ownership patterns and class relations..
v
[4] Neo-Marxist cultural critique treats communication and consumer desire as sites of
domination, not merely reflections of factory ownership. (PDF pp.53-54)
v

claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.

conclude with a qualified political judgment.
CENTRAL FOCUS
Historical Materialism Without Mechanical Determinism
[1] Start with Marxism as scientific socialism responding to capitalist exploitation.
v
[2] Explain base, superstructure, forces of production and relations of production
clearly. (PDF pp.48-49)
v
[3] Show class struggle across historical stages and end with proletarian revolution.
v
[4] Conclude with neo-Marxism: interdependence, ideology critique, alienation,
one-dimensionality and structural analysis. (PDF pp.53-54)
v

its central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.

CENTRAL FOCUS
Class, State, Exploitation and Alienation
[1] Class: private property in the means of production divides society into dominant
(owning) and dependent classes with antagonistic interests, driving conflict across.
v
[2] Alienation: the "Young Marx"/humanist strain of neo-Marxism centres on alienation,
freedom and capitalism's dehumanizing effects on the worker (Gauba, PDF p.47)..
v
[3] Read together: exploitation (surplus value), domination (state as class instrument)
and dehumanization (alienation) are three faces of the same underlying property.
v
[4] Mechanism: when forces of production outgrow existing relations of production, the
relations become a fetter that is broken by revolution, producing a new social.
v

claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.

conclude with a qualified political judgment.

Gramsci and the Frankfurt School
[1] Antonio Gramsci — cross-referenced from Gauba's treatment of hegemony in the
power/authority chapter (Gauba, PDF pp.306, 309-311), rather than from the Marxism.
v
[2] This is a genuine neo-Marxist departure: Gramsci gives relative autonomy to the
superstructure (culture, ideas, civil-society institutions) rather than treating it.
v
[3] Adorno, Horkheimer, Marcuse and Habermas are named together by Gauba as extending
Marxism through critical theory and ideology critique (Gauba, PDF p.53).
v
[4] Mechanism: when forces of production outgrow existing relations of production, the

panels.panel_title: Althusser, Dependency Theory and Classification Cautions
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Althusser, Dependency Theory and Classification Cautions
[1] Louis Althusser represents the "scientific" strain of neo-Marxism, resisting a
purely humanist Marxism and insisting on analysing deep social structures,
especially.
v
[2] Gauba's own text names "dependency theorists" as extending the axis of Marxist
struggle from domestic class conflict to developing nations confronting colonialism.
v
[3] Mechanism: when forces of production outgrow existing relations of production, the
relations become a fetter that is broken by revolution, producing a new social.
v
[4] The Habermas generation caveat (§14.2) and the dependency/world-systems
classification caution (§14.4) are flagged specifically because they are standard
scholarly.
v

panels.panel_title: Objections, Qualified Thesis, Evidence and Doctrine Architecture
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Objections, Qualified Thesis, Evidence and Doctrine Architecture
[1] Premises: (a) private property in the means of production divides society into
antagonistic classes (Gauba, PDF p.47); (b) the mode of production — forces plus.
v
[2] Mechanism: when forces of production outgrow existing relations of production, the
relations become a fetter that is broken by revolution, producing a new social.
v
[3] Conclusion: Marxism's exam-safe verdict is that it remains a powerful structural
theory of exploitation and domination, strengthened rather than refuted by its own.
v
[4] Gauba presents classical Marxism through four main tenets: dialectical materialism,
historical materialism, class conflict and surplus value. (PDF p.48, p.52)
v
